prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, enabling incretin-based therapy of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: B001 was my first choice and is every member's first choice, but unanimity of opening rank is not my argument. The substantive case is that it is a complete arc: gut hormone physiology (Holst), definition of the biology and receptor-mediated actions (Drucker), identification and synthesis of the bioactive GLP-1(7-36) amide (Mojsov), then drugs with large randomized outcome trials showing weight, glycaemic, cardiovascular and renal benefit. The mechanism is understood end to end, independently confirmed over decades, and clinical and societal reach is unmatched among the shortlisted candidates. Recognition now is timely, not premature. I keep a single-achievement prize because the physiology and the three-person cap fit it cleanly, and adding a second part would force a split of the laureate slots that dilutes both.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. The therapies exist because of Knudsen's acylation chemistry for long-acting analogues, and a physiology-only trio rewards the discovery side while omitting the people who made the drugs. The priority around the active peptide (Mojsov versus the Habener group, who are not on the list) is contested and I cannot settle it from the supplied materials. If the committee finds the trio indefensible, the prize stalls on credit rather than science, and a runner-up such as CAR-T or optogenetics could be a safer, though not more meritorious, outcome.

responses.point: Knudsen's work is important but is drug design rather than discovery, so the basic-science trio of Holst, Drucker and Mojsov is preferable, though Mojsov's contribution is decisive yet contested.
responses.response: I largely agree on Holst and Drucker, but I would not dismiss Knudsen as only industrial. Nobel recognition in this field has honoured translational steps when they were conceptually new, and long-acting acylated analogues are what turned a peptide with a minutes-long half-life into a drug. I still land on the basic trio, because the citation can say the physiology enabled the therapy, and because Mojsov's identification of the active form is closer to a discovery than a formulation. Where I differ from you is on confidence: Mojsov's priority is a real open question and should be treated as such, not as settled, and it should be pressed in later rounds.

responses.point: Optogenetics is original and transformative as a causal tool for physiology, and he proposes Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel as one defensible three-person set while noting that Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenbock have substantive claims.
responses.response: I ranked optogenetics third and share the view that its originality and adoption are very high, so I do not discount it as a mere tool. My disagreement is practical: with six credited names, any trio leaves out a decisive contributor, and unlike B001 the exclusion falls on people whose steps (Bamberg's channel electrophysiology, Boyden's neuronal deployment, Miesenbock's earlier concept) are each necessary. That makes it a harder prize to defend as fair than GLP-1, where the exclusion problem is narrower. I would keep it as an alternative, not as the preferred configuration.

responses.point: TNF blockade (B010) and the B and T lymphocyte lineage discovery (B008) are mature, cleanly attributed pairs, and she places Feldmann and Maini second, partly because the recognition is overdue.
responses.response: The clean two-person credit for B010 is a real advantage over my own second choice, and I accept that maturity cuts in its favour. But I place it below CAR-T because TNF blockade, though transformative, is largely clinical validation of a cytokine hypothesis, while engineered T cells introduced a new therapeutic modality. I also doubt that B008 is the right use of a scarce slot this year: it is textbook and the credit is dispersed across Good, Claman, Davies and others, which your own uncertainty acknowledges. I would want the committee to say whether that is a historic correction or an unresolved credit problem.

responses.point: The imatinib story (B004) is a coherent trio of Lydon, Druker and Sawyers that established targeted cancer therapy, mature and not premature, although foundational BCR-ABL work lies outside the credited names; he also notes that CAR-T may overlap in timing with earlier checkpoint-blockade recognition.
responses.response: I agree B004 is mature and that the paradigm has been replicated widely, and I ranked it fifth. My reservation is that a prize to the three credited people is mostly a drug-development citation, with the conceptual discoveries (Philadelphia chromosome, BCR-ABL fusion) credited to others and Rowley deceased, so the citation would carry an explicit gap. On your timing point about checkpoint blockade, I do not think the 2018 prize disqualifies CAR-T, since engineered cells are a different mechanism and modality, but it does argue against pairing the two in a single configuration.

uncertainties: Priority and fair credit for isolating the active GLP-1 peptide (Mojsov versus the Habener group) and whether Knudsen should displace one of the three discovery laureates.
Whether the committee wants a physiology-led or a drug-development-led citation for B001.
If B001 stalls on attribution, which of B017 or B012 gives the more defensible allocation given the omitted contributors (Eshhar for CAR; Bamberg, Boyden, Miesenbock for optogenetics).
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B001, B017 or B012. My spatial transcriptomics co-authorship and my past co-authors (for example Betsholtz, Frisen, Ernfors, Castelo-Branco, Sandberg) are not credited names on any shortlisted ballot, and I will not infer other ties from shared institutions or topics.
